coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay South Block 22 (park)
record.summary: A landscaped lawn with trees on Mission Bay South's plan Block 22; not a formally named park in any source checked. Pier & Point's own satellite review found no building footprint on the site, and a September 2026 on-site visit by Pier & Point confirmed it is already a completed small park rather than still-planned open space, correcting an earlier satellite-only assessment. No independently published source (a city agency, news outlet or landscape-architecture record) naming or dating it was found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: PARTIALLY REAL -- the outer boundary is a real polygonized city block from real street geometry, not hand-traced. No internal A/B split needed (this label is a single block).
notes.digitized_from: Real block boundary: the city block outlined by DataSF's official street centerlines, trimmed back to allow for the full street width.

changes.text: The map notes' lookup of the retired 1998 'COMMON_AREAS' placeholder parcel now cites its DataSF row (blklot 8799TBA3, mapped 1998-07-01, dropped 2005-09-19). UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation map labels a park 'KORET QUAD (22)' (and OCII's November 2024 CAC map is reported to label a completed park 'Koret Quad') at this block, which would contradict 'not a formally named park'; nothing about the block's name, status or geometry was changed because the match has not been confirmed, and the record's open questions and map notes now say so. The NAIP credit names the USDA Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, which the data.gov record names as NAIP's administrator, and the Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural.

changes.text: Mission Bay South Block 22 (park): status corrected from 'planned' to 'complete'. The block had been registered as a future park based on satellite imagery (a landscaped lawn with trees, no dirt, no structure), which fits either a finished small park or an interim-landscaped future site; that ambiguity should have been flagged as a question rather than resolved by assumption. An on-site visit confirmed the park is complete. A follow-up DataSF Assessor parcel and building-footprint check found no structure on the site and traced the main underlying parcel to a retired 1998 'COMMON_AREAS' placeholder plus edge fragments of the scattered UCSF campus parcel. That is consistent with open land, but it was the on-site visit, not this lookup, that settled 'complete' over 'planned'. (The retired parcel is DataSF Parcels blklot 8799TBA3, mapped 1998-07-01 and dropped 2005-09-19; read 2026-09-29.)

open_questions: No independently published source (SF Recreation & Park Department, OCII, news coverage) names or dates this park; the only evidence found is Pier & Point's own satellite-imagery review and its September 2026 on-site confirmation that it is already built, both recorded in the mapping log for this record's shape -- not a substitute for a dated public-record source, so no completion milestone is asserted here.

Pier & Point's earlier DataSF Assessor Parcels/Building Footprints check (recorded in the same mapping log) traced the dominant underlying parcel to a retired 1998 'COMMON_AREAS' placeholder (blklot 8799TBA3, dropped 2005) plus scattered UCSF campus parcel fragments -- consistent with open, non-built land, but that doesn't establish when the current landscaping was actually built.
Not clear whether this block corresponds to any of OCII's lettered/numbered open-space plan parcels (P1-P27) tracked elsewhere in this project; no such label was found for it in any source checked.

Possible identity, not confirmed: UCSF's June 12, 2025 CAC presentation (p.3 map, 'MAP UPDATED: DECEMBER 2024', read directly 2026-09-29) labels a park 'KORET QUAD (22)' in the North Campus, and OCII's Nov 14, 2024 'Mission Bay Future Parks' CAC update (p.2 map) is reported to label a completed park 'Koret Quad' in this block's position, and Wikipedia's Mission Bay article lists Koret Quad among parks complete by fall 2010. Whether this block is Koret Quad still needs to be confirmed before the record is renamed or its 'complete' status is sourced to that map; until then the status rests only on Pier & Point's September 2026 site visit.

record.notes: A Pier & Point site visit (2026-09-19) confirmed that this park is complete. No building footprint here (satellite- and building-footprint-confirmed); the OCII plan's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map designates this block's future land use as park (shown in park-green). No specific project name, developer, or completion date was found.
